overall.normal: Continue routine monitoring and tank maintenance. A Normal result means the pattern resembles the model's reference data; it does not confirm safe water. Follow configured sensor alerts and your farm procedures.
overall.verify: Recheck temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, and turbidity with calibrated or independently verified instruments; inspect the probes and review recent tank changes. Follow any configured safety alert. Do not treat or adjust water based on this ML result alone.

DO.decreasing: Verify the DO reading and probe, then check aerator power, airflow, and water circulation. Review recent feeding and accumulated organic waste, which can increase oxygen demand as it decomposes. Monitor DO and follow your low-oxygen response plan if its separate safety alert triggers.
DO.increasing: Verify the DO reading. Review recent aeration or circulation changes and the time of day; photosynthesis can raise daytime DO, while DO commonly falls overnight. A rising trend alone does not confirm safe water; keep monitoring and follow configured limits.
DO.stable: Verify the DO reading and probe, then check aerator operation and circulation. A stable recent trend can still be unusual relative to the model's reference; follow the separate DO safety alert if triggered.
DO.verify: Verify the DO reading with a reliable meter and inspect the probe, aerator, and circulation. Continue monitoring and follow the separate DO safety alert or farm response plan.

turbidity.increasing: Verify the turbidity probe is clean and consistently positioned. Inspect water clarity, filtration or solids removal, recent feeding, accumulated waste, and tank disturbance. Suspended sediment, organic particles, algae, or plankton can affect turbidity, so the reading alone cannot identify the material. Follow configured limits.
turbidity.decreasing: Verify the probe and review recent filtration, settling, cleaning, or water changes. Lower turbidity alone does not establish that the water or other conditions are safe; continue routine monitoring and follow configured limits.
turbidity.stable: Check probe cleanliness and placement, filtration, and the recent water appearance. A stable trend can still be unusual relative to the model's reference; follow any separate configured alert.
turbidity.verify: Verify the turbidity reading and probe placement, then inspect filtration and recent tank changes. The sensor indicates water clarity, not the identity of suspended material; follow configured limits.

pH.increasing: Confirm the pH with a calibrated meter. Review recent water changes, source water, added materials, and alkalinity, which affects pH buffering. Do not add chemicals based on this ML result alone; follow configured pH limits and farm guidance.
pH.decreasing: Confirm the pH with a calibrated meter. Review recent water changes, source water, added materials, and alkalinity, which affects pH buffering. Do not add chemicals based on this ML result alone; follow configured pH limits and farm guidance.
pH.stable: Confirm the pH with a calibrated meter and inspect the probe. Review recent water changes, source water, alkalinity, and the time-of-day pattern. A stable trend can still be unusual relative to the model's reference; do not chemically adjust from this result alone.
pH.verify: Confirm the pH with a calibrated meter, inspect the probe, and review recent water changes and alkalinity. Avoid chemical adjustment based on this ML result alone; follow configured limits and farm guidance.

temp.increasing: Verify the temperature with a reliable thermometer. Review sunlight or heat exposure, incoming water, and circulation; warmer water can hold less dissolved oxygen. Check DO as well and follow configured temperature or DO alerts.
temp.decreasing: Verify the temperature with a reliable thermometer. Review ambient conditions, incoming water, and circulation, then compare with the operating range chosen for your crayfish species and setup. Follow configured temperature alerts.
temp.stable: Verify the temperature reading and probe placement, then compare it with the operating range chosen for your crayfish species and setup. A stable trend can still be unusual relative to the model's reference; follow configured alerts.
temp.verify: Verify the temperature with a reliable thermometer and review recent ambient conditions, incoming water, and circulation. Compare with the range chosen for your crayfish species and setup; follow configured alerts.

combined_do_turbidity.action: Verify both readings and probes. Check aeration, circulation, filtration or solids removal, and recent feeding, waste, or tank disturbance. Follow either sensor's configured safety alert.

combined_temp_do.action: Verify both readings. Review heat exposure or incoming-water changes, and check aerator operation and circulation. Warm water holds less oxygen at saturation, so monitor DO closely and follow the configured temperature and DO alerts.

combined_ph_do.action: Verify both readings and note the time of day. Photosynthesis and respiration can affect daily pH and DO patterns in ponds. Continue monitoring and follow the separate pH and DO safety alerts.

redclaw_qld.title: Business Queensland: Redclaw crayfish aquaculture
redclaw_qld.scope: Species-specific context for Cherax quadricarinatus, primarily in earthen ponds; do not transfer its numeric guidance to another species or tank without local validation.

ras_qld.title: Business Queensland: Recirculating aquaculture systems
ras_qld.scope: General recirculating-aquaculture system and filtration context; inspect the installed system rather than infer failure from a sensor pattern.

usgs_do.title: U.S. Geological Survey: Dissolved Oxygen and Water
usgs_do.scope: Temperature affects oxygen solubility; photosynthesis and decomposition can influence dissolved oxygen.

usgs_turbidity.title: U.S. Geological Survey: Turbidity and Water
usgs_turbidity.scope: Turbidity is affected by suspended inorganic and organic matter, algae, and plankton; it does not identify a specific cause.

monitoring_usgs.title: Wagner et al. (2006), Guidelines and standard procedures for continuous water-quality monitors
monitoring_usgs.scope: Quality assurance, calibration, fouling checks, and maintenance for continuous water-quality monitoring.

buffering_msu.title: Mississippi State University Extension: pH and Alkalinity
buffering_msu.scope: Alkalinity buffers pH; pond pH can vary with biological activity and time of day. Fish-pond advice is general context, not a crayfish-tank treatment prescription.

ufifas_aeration.title: UF/IFAS Extension: The Role of Aeration in Pond Management
ufifas_aeration.scope: Pond aeration and water mixing can support dissolved oxygen management; practices must suit the actual production system.

ufifas_do.title: UF/IFAS Extension: Dissolved Oxygen for Fish Production
ufifas_do.scope: Aquaculture pond DO cycles and oxygen demand from excess feed and decaying organic matter; species-specific limits still apply.
